original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

scope_change_reason: The card is narrowed to one concrete construction: replace contiguous rank-2/rank-3 child products in the selected trace by their block-diagonal direct sum, with child side at most 16. The complete chronological interval family is optimized under a zero-charge relaxation; no physical supplier or changed decoder support is asserted.
actual_scope: Exact mixed-rank direct-sum identity and maximum disjoint interval packing over uninterrupted rank-2/rank-3 climbs in both orientations of the selected width-73 gauge44 provider, with every gathering, routing, interface, hosting, precision, and restoration expense set to zero.
bottleneck_link: Larger rank children reduce recursive moment per unit of paid rank mass. The selected card requires at least a five-percent ceiling gain, while this trace permits only a bounded number of chronological mixed-rank replacements even before physical charges.
stop_rule: Stop after pinning and scanning both provider orientations, enumerating all nontrivial contiguous rank-2/rank-3 intervals of total rank at most 16, optimizing disjoint intervals at the exact five-percent target with certified enclosures, and checking the diagonal product and failure controls. Do not move calls across non-phase events or attempt a physical interface after the zero-charge screen misses the gate.
evidence: Both orientations contain 641 runs and 850 rank-2/rank-3 calls; there are 341 nontrivial merge intervals and 1,191 windows including no-op singletons. The optimizer selects 162 blocks, preserves local mass 5,586, and yields ceiling upper endpoint 0.001764844128533 (4.425304% above the selected endpoint). A certified upper bound on all zero-charge savings leaves target relaxation above one by more than 0.0000270103.
author: Cinna Davis, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents.
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance in source exploration, mathematical formulation, exact optimizer and symbolic controls, verification, and package writing. Selected-word construction credit remains with its original authors.

open_questions.question: Can nonconsecutive mixed-rank blocks be assembled with a fully charged operand-lifetime and restoration schedule?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Nonconsecutive packing could recover more of the rank-2/rank-3 mass, but copies, interfaces, output preservation, and dirty restoration may consume the remaining ceiling margin.
open_questions.first_step: Find a source representation that maps each child event to its exact operand-ready/use lifetime and mutable output owner, then price one buffered mixed block end to end.
open_questions.blocked_by: The pinned local-program trace records child order and rank but not a complete physical scratch-memory lifetime or restoration contract.
